lessons.title: Preparing to harvest a trial
lessons.html:
Preparing to harvest a trial

A seed trial compares cultivars or breeding lines in small plots. The harvest gives the yield and grain data that decide which entries move forward. A whole season of work depends on harvesting every plot correctly, keeping samples separate and recording accurately.

Check the trial is ready

  • The crop must be physiologically mature and dry enough to harvest. For maize, this is often checked by grain moisture; for wheat or soybeans by pods and ears being dry and seeds hard.
  • The trial manager decides the harvest date. All plots in a trial should be harvested on the same day where possible, so results are fair.
  • Walk the trial and check plot labels and markers against the field plan. Replace missing labels from the plan only.
  • Note plots with problems, such as animal damage, lodging or missing plants, and record them before harvest.

Prepare equipment

  • Plot combine or hand harvesting tools (sickles, knives, bags), depending on the trial.
  • Clean the plot combine fully before the trial and check the weighing and moisture system is calibrated.
  • Pre-printed, numbered bags or barcode labels for each plot, sorted in harvest order.
  • Data sheets or tablets, scale, moisture meter.
  • Trailers or crates to carry samples.

Prepare the team

Brief the team on the harvest order, how plots are cut and bagged, and who records the data. Agree who will check labels before each plot is harvested.

Safety

Plot combines and tractors are dangerous. Only trained operators may drive them. Never clear a blockage while the machine is running; switch off and remove the key. Keep people away from moving parts. Sickles and knives must be carried safely. Wear a hat, gloves and dust mask in dry dusty crops, and drink plenty of water.

lessons.title: Harvesting the trial
lessons.html:
Harvesting the trial

Every plot is a separate sample. The golden rule is: one plot, one bag, one label, and no mixing.

Hand harvesting

  1. Check the plot label against the bag label before you start.
  2. Harvest only the rows and length in the protocol. Often only the middle rows are harvested, because border rows are affected by neighbouring plots.
  3. Count plants or ears if the protocol requires.
  4. Put all harvested material in the bag with that plot's label. Put a second label inside the bag.
  5. Close the bag and put it in order on the trailer.
  6. Pick up every ear or head that fell to the ground from the harvested rows.

Plot combine harvesting

  1. Drive into the plot at the right point; harvest the set length.
  2. Let the machine clear completely between plots so seed from one plot does not go into the next.
  3. Weigh and measure moisture automatically or collect the seed into the labelled bag.
  4. Check that the plot number in the combine's data matches the field plan.

Recording

DataExample
Plot numberFrom label and plan
Plot weightKilograms of grain
Grain moisturePercentage
Plant or ear countIf required
NotesLodging, damage, missing plants

Write data at the plot, not later. If something goes wrong, for example a bag tears or seed spills, note it at once.

Before moving to the next plot, the checker reads the next plot number aloud from the field plan and the harvester confirms it from the label in the field. This simple two-person check catches most mix-ups before they happen. At the end of each range, count the bags against the plan before moving on.

lessons.title: Completing the harvest process
lessons.html:
Completing the harvest process

After the trial is harvested, samples and data must be checked, processed and stored, and equipment must be cleaned.

Checking samples

  • Count bags against the field plan. Every plot should have a bag, unless the plot was abandoned and recorded.
  • Check that labels are readable and match the data sheet.
  • Report any missing or doubtful samples to the trial manager immediately.

Handling samples

  1. Take samples to the drying or processing area as instructed.
  2. Dry samples in their bags if needed. Do not mix or open bags carelessly.
  3. Shell or thresh hand-harvested samples one at a time. Clean the sheller or thresher between samples.
  4. Weigh shelled grain and measure moisture.
  5. Take sub-samples for quality tests if the protocol says so, labelled with the plot number.
  6. Store samples in a cool, dry, rodent-free place in plot order.

Data

  • Capture data into the trial spreadsheet or database. Check for typing errors by comparing with the field sheets.
  • Look for strange numbers, such as a plot weight ten times higher than the others, and check them.
  • Keep the original field sheets.
  • Hand the data to the trial manager for analysis.

Equipment and field

Clean the plot combine, shellers and tools, and store them. Report damage or faults. Remove labels, pegs and markers from the field after the manager approves. Leave the field tidy for the farmer or station.

Key points

  • Harvest only when the trial manager confirms the crop is ready.
  • Check plot labels against the plan before harvesting each plot.
  • One plot, one bag, one label; never mix samples.
  • Clean machines between plots and between samples.
  • Record data at the plot and check it before handing it in.
